headline: ESCONDIDA PARTIALLY RESTARTS AFTER FATAL ACCIDENT — SUPERVISORS' UNION VOTING ON BHP CONTRACT THIS WEEK
snippet: BHP's Escondida copper mine — the world's largest at 1.3 million tonnes per year — began progressively resuming operations around September 29 after a full halt triggered by a fatal front-end loader accident on September 23. Simultaneously, the mine's supervisors' union is holding a contract vote between September 28-30, with leadership recommending rejection of BHP's offer, raising the prospect of a second labor disruption even as physical operations slowly recover. For copper investors, Escondida's restart trajectory and the supervisors' vote outcome are the most important near-term catalysts: Chile already has Centinela in mandatory mediation with a legal strike window opening October 13, and both mines together represent a potential dual-supply shock to a country providing roughly 27% of global mined copper. Copper futures remain elevated near $6.53–$6.70/lb.

headline: URANIUM ENERGY FY2026: 157% Q4 PRODUCTION SURGE TO 82,744 LB — $93.13/LB REALIZED PRICE, $753M LIQUID, ZERO DEBT
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE American: UEC) reported September 29 fiscal 2026 results for the year ended July 31: Q4 combined production at Christensen Ranch and Burke Hollow surged 157% over Q3 to 82,744 lb U₃O₈, with total cost per pound of $36.54 — well below the $93.13/lb peer-leading realized selling price. FY2026 totals: 229,294 lb U₃O₈ produced; revenue $37.3 million; gross profit $16.9 million. The company holds $753 million in liquid assets including $495 million cash with zero debt, while strategically building physical inventory ahead of what it forecasts as a 4-million-lb/year US government domestic uranium requirement from 2030. Burke Hollow completed its first full quarter of operations. For uranium mining investors, UEC's combination of multi-mine growth, sub-$40/lb costs against $90+ spot, and fortress balance sheet is the clearest expression of the US uranium thesis in a single annual result.

headline: OSISKO METALS GASPÉ: 211M @ 0.59% CU INCLUDING 28.5M @ 2.31% CU — 500M WEST OF 2026 RESOURCE MODEL
snippet: Osisko Metals Incorporated (TSX-V: OM) reported September 28 drill hole 30-1243 intersected 211.5 metres averaging 0.59% copper at the Gaspé Copper Project in eastern Québec, including a 28.5-metre high-grade interval averaging 2.31% copper and 11.8 g/t silver. The intersection sits 500–600 metres west of the current 2026 mineral resource estimate model boundary — out-of-pit expansion territory. Earlier 2026 holes returned 256m at 0.85% Cu (September 10) and 312m at 0.56% Cu (August 20), establishing a pattern of thick, high-grade intervals systematically expanding the deposit's footprint at depth and strike. Gaspé is one of Canada's most significant copper development projects by scale; for retail investors tracking TSX-V copper names, the consistency of wide, above-threshold intercepts outside the existing resource boundary is the strongest possible signal that the next resource update will show meaningful growth.

headline: AMERICAN RARE EARTHS HALLECK CREEK FS DRILLING: 191M @ 3,951 PPM TREO — CERTIFIED ASSAYS FROM COWBOY STATE MINE
snippet: American Rare Earths Limited (ASX: ARR) released certified assay results September 29 from the first six of 18 Feasibility Study-grade HQ core drill holes at the Cowboy State Mine, Red Mountain, within the Halleck Creek Rare Earth Project in Wyoming. The headline interval is 191.11 metres at a weighted average of 3,951 ppm Total Rare Earth Oxide (TREO) with a peak of 6,939 ppm TREO; a pooled average across 386 geological intervals grades 3,497 ppm TREO. Halleck Creek is advancing toward a formal Feasibility Study against a backdrop of Wyoming's favourable mining permitting environment and the Trump administration's policy push to develop domestic Western rare earth supply. For investors tracking REE supply chain stocks, the combination of broad continuous mineralisation and certified FS-grade assays is a clear step forward — the remaining 12 holes are pending.

headline: GOLD DRIFTS NEAR SEVEN-WEEK LOW AS JOLTS DUE TODAY — PCE WEDNESDAY, PAYROLLS FRIDAY; 70% OCTOBER HIKE ODDS
snippet: Gold lingered near a seven-week low around $4,115–$4,150/oz on September 29-30 as markets braced for a packed week of US economic data: August JOLTS job openings (due Tuesday), August PCE inflation (Wednesday), and the September employment report (Friday). The CME FedWatch Tool shows 70% probability of a 25bp hike in October — the Fed already tightened to 3.75–4.00% on September 16 in a unanimous vote, and 16 of 18 officials signalled further tightening. US 10-year yields pushed above 5.20%, a 20-year high, weighing on gold's appeal. For junior gold mining investors, this week's data releases are the near-term pivot: softer prints could signal that Monday's break below $4,200 has already priced enough tightening; hotter readings extend the compression on project economics and developer valuations into Q4.

headline: SILVER MORE VULNERABLE THAN GOLD: COT POSITIONING GAP SIGNALS FORCED SELLING RISK AHEAD OF PCE AND NFP
snippet: A September 29 FX Street analysis of Commitments of Traders data shows silver's net speculative positioning is at a wider premium to neutral than gold's, leaving it more exposed to forced liquidation if this week's PCE or payrolls data reinforce October rate hike expectations. Silver fell only 0.11% on September 29 while gold bounced more sharply, but the COT structure suggests silver could lead any downside move on hot macro prints. Silver sits at $60.80–$61.05/oz, down 8.5% over the past month despite being 30% higher year-over-year. For investors in silver mining stocks, the near-term positioning risk is real even as the fundamental case remains intact — six consecutive years of supply deficit, rising industrial demand from AI data centres, and physical investment demand all support a higher long-term price. The gold-silver ratio at ~68 remains well below the historical average of 78–80.

headline: EMPEROR + GLOBEX — DUQUESNE WEST, QUÉBEC: ADDITIONAL GOLD INTERSECTIONS IN 20,479M ABITIBI DRILL PROGRAM
snippet: Emperor Metals Corp. (TSX-V: AUOZ) and joint-venture partner Globex Mining Enterprises reported September 29 additional gold drill hole assays from the Duquesne West Property in Duparquet Township, Québec — the prolific Abitibi greenstone camp that also hosts Osisko Mining's Duparquet Gold Project. The program has now completed 20,479 metres of new diamond drilling plus approximately 7,884 metres of targeted resampling of unsampled historical core, for a combined program scale of over 28,000 metres. Duparquet's polymetallic Abitibi geology has historically produced multiple significant gold intercepts in a single drill program; Emperor's rolling assay releases indicate an ongoing systematic advance through the system. For retail investors tracking Québec gold explorers, the Duparquet camp is one of the highest-pedigree jurisdictions in Canada, and the historical core resampling component adds upside without incremental drilling cost.

headline: SABLE RESOURCES — MOXICO FUNDS 3,500M DRILL AT EL FIERRO, SAN JUAN ARGENTINA IN EARN-IN DEAL
snippet: Sable Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: SAE) announced September 29 that Moxico Resources will fully fund a 3,500-metre drill program at the El Fierro gold-silver project in San Juan Province, Argentina, as part of an earn-in agreement. Moxico's funding commitment means zero cash-call dilution for Sable during the program. San Juan is Argentina's premier mining jurisdiction, home to several significant gold-silver operations and development projects; El Fierro is an early-stage target being drill-tested for the first time under the earn-in structure. For TSX-V gold-silver investors, earn-in funding arrangements from established operators signal that a technically credible partner has evaluated the target and committed real capital — the most meaningful pre-drill validation a junior property can receive.

headline: GOLD MOUNTAIN (ASX: GMN) — IRAJUBA REE DRILLING: 192 SAMPLES CONFIRM UP TO 4,599 PPM TREO IN BRAZIL
snippet: Gold Mountain Limited (ASX: GMN) released September 30 drill results from five vertical diamond drill holes at the Irajuba Prospect (IR-1 Target) in Brazil: 192 geological samples confirming broad, consistent rare earth element mineralisation across the weathered regolith profile, with headline intercepts reaching 4,599 ppm TREO. The project is now advancing to metallurgical testing at ALS and ANSTO. The Irajuba weathered profile is consistent with ionic adsorption clay-style REE mineralisation — the same deposit type that has historically supplied China's heavy rare earth elements (dysprosium, terbium, neodymium), which are disproportionately critical to electric vehicle motors and defence applications. Metallurgical test results will determine whether the Irajuba mineralogy supports low-cost extraction. For investors focused on non-Chinese REE supply, early-stage ionic adsorption discoveries outside Southeast Asia are increasingly strategic.

headline: GOLD MINERS STILL UNDERVALUED: 91% EARNINGS GROWTH, 37% MARGINS — BUT P/NAV DISCOUNTS PERSIST AT $4,150 GOLD
snippet: A late September 2026 analysis argues that even with gold near $4,150/oz, major gold producers trade below fair value on net asset value measures — P/NAV multiples remain compressed at many seniors despite 91% year-on-year earnings growth, operating margins around 37%, and record free cash flow. Consensus 2026 revenue growth is driven almost entirely by price (+21% YoY), while production is down just 0.6%. The analysis highlights Newmont (global diversification, ongoing buybacks), Agnico Eagle (stable jurisdictions, ~40% margins), and Coeur Mining (26.8% margin expansion) as specific undervaluation opportunities. For retail investors tracking junior miners: if seniors trade at a discount to intrinsic value at current gold prices, developers and explorers with quality assets sit at an even steeper discount — the leverage case for quality juniors has rarely been better-supported by fundamentals.

headline: COPPER DROPS 2.3% AS FED HIKE BETS LIFT THE DOLLAR — FUTURES NEAR $6.53/LB DESPITE CHILE SUPPLY SHOCK
snippet: Copper futures fell 2.29% on September 28-29 as rising US 10-year yields above 5.20% — a 20-year high — pushed the US dollar higher, making dollar-priced base metals more expensive for overseas buyers. COMEX copper retreated from its September 8 record of $6.83/lb to approximately $6.53/lb. The decline comes despite the most concentrated Chilean supply disruption in years: Escondida halted after a fatal accident (September 23), Centinela's union in mandatory mediation with a legal strike window opening October 13. For investors in copper-focused juniors, the tension between dollar-driven price weakness and a fundamental supply shock is creating heightened volatility. The upcoming PCE (Wednesday) and US payrolls (Friday) data will determine which force — macro or physical — dominates copper pricing into the October contract.
